TOM GREEN, AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                     §




  REPLY BRIEF OF JOHN BRADLEY, LAZY S RANCH, REGARDING REMANDED
                 PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13


TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

COMES NOW, John B. Bradley, of the Lazy S Ranch a pro se Intervenor respectfully
files TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

This reply brief is respectfully submitted by John Bradley, a pro se Intervenor and owner
of the Lazy S Ranch. Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 35, this brief replies to the
Applicants’ arguments on remanded Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13. The
Applicants’ "Directory of Evidence" fails to cure the fatal defects in their application. It
merely points back to the same broken evidentiary record that already led the
Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) to recommend denial. The application rests on a
faulty foundation—the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP)—and must be denied.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: A PATCHED FOUNDATION IS STILL A BROKEN
FOUNDATION
The Commission remanded this matter because the Proposal for Decision (PFD) did not
explicitly answer whether Import Path 2 is necessary for reliability (Issue 11) or justified
by congestion savings (Issue 13). The Applicants’ response is to simply re-submit


59475 – REPLY BRIEF REMANDED PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13
                                         Page 1 of 5
 evidence that the ALJs already found unpersuasive. They have not, and cannot, prove
their case on the existing record.

   1. On Issue 11, they still fail to prove the project is necessary to meet mandatory
      reliability standards. They confuse “meeting” a standard with being “required” by
      it and base their claim on the PBRP’s load forecasts, which the record shows are
      overstated and invalid.

   2. On Issue 13, they continue to claim exemption from economic analysis while
      simultaneously cherry-picking economic data points on congestion savings, a
      contradiction that proves they have not met the requirements for an economic
      project.

The ALJs’ initial recommendation of denial was correct. The record shows the
Applicants have failed their burden of proof on both counts.

ARGUMENT AND AUTHORITIES

I. APPLICANTS FAIL TO PROVE THE PROJECT IS NECESSARY UNDER ISSUE 11

To bypass a full economic review, a project must be "necessary to meet state or federal
reliability standards." The Applicants have failed to meet this strict requirement.

A. Applicants Confuse “Meeting” a Standard with Being “Required” by It.

The Applicants’ core argument is that their project was modeled consistent with NERC
Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1. But as the PFD correctly found, this does not prove
the project is necessary. Building a four-lane bridge across a dry creek bed might meet
structural engineering codes, but that does not prove the bridge was ever needed.

The PFD originally found that Applicants presented this project as one to import power,
not one necessary to fix a specific reliability violation (PFD, FOF 224). In their response
to the remand, Applicants still fail to identify any mandatory NERC or ERCOT standard
that would be violated but for the construction of Import Path 2. They offer only
generalized claims of improving transfer capability, which is not the same as preventing
a specific, identified violation.

B. The Project’s Foundational Load Forecasts are Unreliable.

The entire reliability claim rests on the PBRP, which in turn rests on speculative load
forecasts. The evidentiary record proves this foundation is broken:

   1. Outdated and Overstated Forecasts: The PFD correctly identifies that the S&P
      Global study underpinning the PBRP’s load projections is overstated and
      outdated (PFD, FOF 107-109). The Commission itself recognized this when it
                                  REPLY BRIEF REMANDED PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13
                                                                    PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                                                             SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                                                                 Page 2 of 5
        directed ERCOT to apply a material discount to similar officer-letter and data
       center loads in the 2025 RTP (PFD, FOF 89). Applying this same discount to the
       PBRP load would eliminate at least 3,571 MW of the supposed need (PFD, FOF
       92), fundamentally undermining the justification for a project with a 5,270 MW
       capacity (PFD, FOF 93).

   2. New Permian Generation: The record documents over 25,000 MW of new,
      planned gas generation in and around the Permian Basin (PFD, FOF 143, 145).
      This new local generation directly addresses the purported need for importing
      power but was not properly considered by Applicants.

Applicants cannot claim their project is necessary for reliability when the very "need"
they cite is based on speculative forecasts that have been contradicted by updated,
more realistic methodologies and changing market conditions.
II. APPLICANTS FAIL TO PROVIDE ECONOMIC JUSTIFICATION UNDER ISSUE 13

If a project is not necessary for reliability, it must be justified on economic grounds by
proving a net benefit to consumers. Applicants have failed this test.

The ALJs correctly found that Applicants "did not submit the estimated cost of the
facilities to consumers or the estimated congestion cost savings" (PFD, FOF 226). In
their initial briefing, Applicants stated that "reliability projects are expressly exempt from
the economic tests, including the congestion cost savings test" (Applicants' Exceptions,
p. 164).

Now, on remand, they reverse course and point to evidence of congestion savings to
answer Issue 13. This contradiction is telling. Applicants cannot claim exemption from
economic analysis and then, when directed to answer for it, cherry-pick favorable data
points without conducting the full, required analysis. If they wish to claim economic
benefits, they must prove the project offers a net positive economic benefit to
consumers under a complete production-cost-savings test. They have not done so. The
record is devoid of any such analysis, leaving ratepayers to foot a multi-billion-dollar bill
with no evidence of a net financial benefit.

CONCLUSION AND PRAYER

The remand has only confirmed the original flaws in this application. The Applicants
have failed to demonstrate that Import Path 2 is either necessary for reliability or
economically justified. The project is a structure built on a broken foundation.

Wherefore, premises considered, John Bradley respectfully requests that the
Administrative Law Judges issue a supplemental PFD that:

                                   REPLY BRIEF REMANDED PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13
                                                                     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                                                              SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                                                                   Page 3 of 5
    1. Finds that Applicants have failed to meet their burden of proof to show the
      proposed project is necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards under
      Issue 11.

   2. Finds that Applicants have failed to provide the required evidence of estimated
      congestion cost savings or net economic benefit to consumers under Issue 13.

   3. Maintains and reaffirms the original recommendation to DENY the application for
      a Certificate of Convenience and Necessity for Import Path 2.
Respectfully submitted,

Date Signed: October 2, 2026



Respectfully submitted,

John B. Bradley
